claims: C1 the system level sits below root and above developer, user, and guideline in the authority hierarchy
C2 system-level instructions can only be supplied by OpenAI
C3 OpenAI may supply system-level instructions through this Model Spec or through detailed policies
C4 OpenAI may supply system-level instructions via a system message

concepts.name: system_authority
concepts.gloss: the system level of instruction authority: rules set by OpenAI that can be transmitted or overridden through system messages, but cannot be overridden by developers or users
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the node's NEEDS contract assigns (mechanical licence correction under DECISION_licence_textual.md, 2026-08-16)

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the node's NEEDS contract assigns (mechanical licence correction under DECISION_licence_textual.md, 2026-08-16)

concepts.name: system_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction that carries system-level authority
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of system-level instructions, so a class of instructions at that level must exist

concepts.name: supplied_by_openai
concepts.gloss: the instruction is supplied by OpenAI rather than by a developer or user

concepts.name: supplied_via_model_spec_or_policies
concepts.gloss: the instruction is supplied through this Model Spec or through detailed policies

concepts.name: supplied_via_system_message
concepts.gloss: the instruction is supplied via a system message
